title: Trapping Rain Water
description:
Each nonnegative number in height is the height of a unit-width column. After rain, water can rest in the low spaces between taller columns. Return the total number of unit squares of trapped water.

At a position, the water level is bounded by the highest column to its left and the highest to its right; the smaller boundary wins. This makes the problem a useful exercise in tracking what is known from each end without simulating rainfall.

Example 1:

Input: height = [0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1]
Output: 6

Example 2:

Input: height = [4,2,0,3,2,5]
Output: 9

Example 3:

Input: height = [3,0,3]
Output: 3

Constraints:

  • 0 <= height.length <= 20,000
  • 0 <= height[i] <= 100,000
  • An empty profile or one without two enclosing columns holds no water.

exampleTestCases.explanation: Several dips hold a total of six units.
The interior gaps collectively hold nine units.
The middle column is three units below either boundary.
